packages.author: spacemeowx2, DefenderOfHyrule
packages.details:
ldn_mitm is a sysmodule that replaces the Switch's ldn service and redirects local-wireless discovery over LAN networking.

It allows games that normally communicate through local wireless to work over a network connection, and is commonly used together with switch-lan-play for online play with supported local-wireless titles.

packages.name: sys-patch
packages.title: sys-patch
packages.description: Apply system patches automatically at boot.
packages.author: btc08gh, impeeza
packages.details:
sys-patch is a sysmodule that automatically applies fs, es, ldr, nifm, and nim patches when the system boots.

It can patch both sysMMC and emuMMC and includes an overlay for changing configuration options and checking which patches were successfully applied. The overlay distinguishes between patches applied by sys-patch and patches that were already present from another source.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-patch/config.ini`, where you can control sysMMC and emuMMC patching, logging, and version-pattern behavior.

Because sys-patch modifies low-level system behavior, it is best suited for advanced users who understand Atmosphere and firmware compatibility.

packages.author: tico
packages.details:
tico is an emulator frontend with support for multiple retro systems through independently maintained emulator cores.

It provides a customizable home interface, game-library browsing, cover and artwork management, RetroAchievements integration, touch support, and built-in management for supported emulator cores.

Additional emulator cores and supporting files can be installed or updated from within tico.
packages.changelog:
0.8.2

tico 0.8.2 fixes RetroAchievements sign-in, which failed for everyone on 0.8.1 with "Sign-in failed".

> [!NOTE]
> tico 0.8.2 works with the same 3.0.0 emulators as 0.8.0 and 0.8.1. Nothing to reinstall.

## RetroAchievements

- **Sign-in works again.** RetroAchievements now refuses sign-ins from apps that present themselves as a web browser, which tico did. tico now identifies itself as tico.
- **tico signs in by itself.** If your password is saved but games aren't signed in, tico signs in in the background after you pick your account, with no need to open Settings or start a game. You'll see "Signed in as …" once it works.
- If RetroAchievements turns down your password, tico doesn't try it again until you change it. If there's no connection, it tries again a minute later.
- When RetroAchievements refuses a sign-in without saying why, Settings › Accounts shows the server's answer (for example "HTTP 403") instead of only "Sign-in failed".

Achievements inside games were not affected: emulators already reached RetroAchievements correctly once tico had signed in.

## Updating

Open the Store in tico and install the tico update, or copy `tico.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/tico/` (over the old one).

If your account showed **Sign-in failed** in 0.8.1, you don't need to do anything: start tico 0.8.2 and it signs in by itself.

packages.description: Switch between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.
packages.author: Nextendo Network
packages.details:
Prelude is a homebrew application for switching between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.

Nextendo mode configures the Atmosphere files and patches needed to connect supported games and services to Nextendo Network. Nintendo mode removes Prelude's changes and restores the console's normal Nintendo network configuration.

packages.name: sys-dock
packages.title: sys-dock
packages.description: Enable higher docked display bandwidth and refresh rates.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
sys-dock is a sysmodule that patches docked DisplayPort link training to allow higher-bandwidth display modes and higher refresh rates.

It's primarily intended for use alongside FPSLocker, especially on OLED models where the default docked DisplayPort configuration can limit available refresh rates. The included overlay lets you enable or disable individual DisplayPort patches and see which patches are currently active.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-dock/config.ini` and can be edited manually or through the overlay.

Because sys-dock changes low-level dock and display behavior, incompatible docks, displays, cables, or patch combinations may cause display corruption, instability, or other unexpected behavior.

packages.changelog:
v0.7.23

v0.7.23: firmware 23.5.0, and a newer firmware no longer stops the console

**Fixes**
- **Firmware 23.5.0: no more crash at boot** (#83, #87, #90, #99): the sysmodule is now built against Atmosphère 1.12.2, which knows 23.5.0. v0.7.22 and older were built against 1.12.0, whose library stops any program on a firmware newer than it knows - a fatal error (std::abort, 0100000000000C20) on every boot. Update Atmosphère to 1.12.2 first. Tested by users on firmware 21.1.0 and 23.0.1 (and an Atmosphère 1.12.2 build on 23.5.0).
- **A newer firmware no longer stops the console**: from this version on, when the console runs a firmware newer than the build knows, Switch Frame Tap boots without streaming and the app and viewer say to update (Setup > Allow untested firmware tries anyway).
- **Games with many buffers the size of their screen** (#70, Maestro): the stream finds which buffers hold the picture by watching them change; Maestro has 95 of them and the stream looked at the first 48 only, so it showed a wrong one (violet noise). It now looks at up to 96, reading the same amount per frame as before. When it still can't tell, the log says why.

**Viewers**
- **Playback volume** (thanks @myaumura, #85, #84): Settings > Sound > Playback volume, 0-100 %, saved. Recordings and the Switch's own volume are not changed.
- **Smoother under load** (thanks @Laliukz, #92): the packet queue hands buffers over instead of copying them, and the viewer's threads run at a higher priority. On Windows and Linux (OpenGL), **Y** sets an FSR/NIS render scale (150/200/300 %) and **F9** the sharpness. On Windows, the previous session's log is kept as viewer.prev.log.
- **USB on Macs** (#49): when USB reads fail, the viewer clears a stalled connection and, after 8 errors in a row, opens the Switch again as after a pulled cable.

Note: "Sound in no-record games" has no patch for 23.5.0 yet (exelix11/dvr-patches) - on 23.5.0 those games stay silent for now.

**Updating:** open the Switch app's **Updates** page (or unzip `switch-frame-tap-0.7.23-switch.zip` over the SD card root) and restart the console. Settings are kept. On firmware 23.5.0 with v0.7.22 installed the console stops at boot: unzip this version onto the SD card from a PC. The PC viewers and the Android app offer the update when they open.

---
<sub>Switch Frame Tap is free and open source. If you would like to support it: [buymeacoffee.com/papux200](https://buymeacoffee.com/papux200)</sub>

SaltyNX is a background process that enables runtime file and code modification in retail games.

packages.changelog:
2.1.4

- NVN games should boot now faster
- Fix compatibility with OpenGL games that don't use uniform buffers for shaders (f.e. Dragon Quest Builders)
- Fix compatibility with OpenGL games having small thread stack on swap thread (f.e. Dragon Quest Builders)
- Fix compatibility with NVN games reserving 2GB for GPU use (Old Lego games)
  - Old NVN games have offset stored as signed 32-bit value so our new reservation was causing overflow in their case, Core now reserves buffer for shaders before game does it for GPU
- Fix compatibility with games using `nn::diag::GetRequiredBufferSizeForGetAllModuleInfo()` manually that abort when output is 0 (f.e. Hitman Absolution 1.4_107768, older updates don't use it)
- Increase size of NVNSampler to fit data expected by old and new NVN (code had size 0x30, old NVN used 0x60)

packages.changelog:
1.12.2

**1.12.2** is Atmosphère's ninety-fifth official release.

**Please be sure to update fusee when upgrading to 1.12.2**. fusee-primary no longer exists, and will not work any more.

**Note**: `fusee.bin` was updated on 2026/11/13 at 12:08 PM PDT to fix a failure to apply a nogc patch on 23.5.0. The updated fusee has a sha256 hash prefix of `E8B8D926D5...`

With thanks to the @switchbrew team, Atmosphère 1.12.2 is bundled with [hbl](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbloader) 2.4.5, and [hbmenu](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbmenu) 3.6.1.

The following was changed since the last release:
* Basic support was added for 23.5.0.
* General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

And the following was changed in 1.12.0:
* Support was added for 23.0.0.
* Special thanks to @alula for handling the implementation of several kernel changes.
    * The console should boot and atmosphère should be fully functional.
    * **Please note**: As a result of changes made to nintendo's software in 23.0.0, there is even less memory available for custom system modules.
        * The amount of memory we can steal from the applet pool has been reduced beyond 7MB and we can no longer launch browser applets (e.g.: eshop) without crashing.
        * To compensate for this, a set of patches for the browser applets has been introduced.
            * Thanks to the redesign of the browser applets in 22.0.0 there are only 3 applets we need to worry about: systemWeb, openWeb and LibAppletOff.
            * With the added burden of maintaining patches for these applets, we can reclaim around 9MB of reserved memory by patching out their allocations.
            * This memory is provably unused and stealing it should not affect the browser applets in any way as the applets themselves tag it as reserved and never access it.
            * As a result, the memory available for custom system modules has been experimentally increased to 16MB.
            * Preliminary testing has seemingly shown no downsides to the overall functioning of the OS and the browser applets in particular.
            * Nonetheless, please report any issues you may face to ensure no edge cases have been missed and to determine if the memory amount needs to be adjusted. 
            * These patches may be deprecated at any point in the future if a better solution is devised.     
    * `exosphère` was updated to reflect the latest official secure monitor behavior.
        * A new ConfigItem was added to the secure monitor for the first time since firmware 5.0.0.
    * `mesosphère` was updated to reflect the latest official kernel behavior.
        * The kernel now supports a 42bit wide address space.
        * A new memory region dubbed ShadowStack has been introduced.
        * Kernel RNG was changed to CTR-DRBG.
    * `boot` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior and to implement a previously missing change.
        * The way battery i2c shutdown was being enabled changed in firmware 18.0.0 and we missed it.
        * It is possible this might have been related to a known battery draining issue reported to have started around firmware 18.0.0. Further testing will be needed to confirm.
    * `loader` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `erpt` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `pgl` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
    * `ro` was updated to reflect the latest official behavior.
        * NROs can now be lz4 frame compressed.
* ZBIC compresison/decompression has been properly implemented. Applications using it should now launch and work properly.
* A dockerfile has been added to atmosphère (thanks @alula).
* R_DISCARD macro has been adopted across the entire codebase where applicable. This finishes the work started in version 1.10.0 and eliminates the nodiscard warnings during compilation.
* General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

For information on the featureset supported by 1.12, please see [the official release notes](https://github.com/Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere/releases/tag/1.12.0).

packages.title: sys-tune
packages.description: Background audio player.
packages.author: HookedBehemoth, ppkantorski
packages.details:
sys-tune is a background audio player with an Ultrahand overlay for controlling playback.

It supports MP3, FLAC, and WAV audio, playlist browsing, seeking, shuffle and repeat modes, persistent playback settings, per-title behavior, and separate control over music and game audio volume.

Music can be played from the SD card and managed without leaving the currently running game or application. sys-tune can also be configured for HOME Menu background music and title-specific playback behavior.

Because audio playback can interfere with sleep mode or titles that heavily use the system audio renderer, pause playback or stop the service if you encounter audio or sleep-related issues.

packages.changelog:
1.7.1

# pipensx 1.7.1

Changes since the last published GitLab release, 1.6.6.

## Catalog and game details

- Search ranks close title matches and compares related releases.
- Catalog cards show cached peer counts, collections, and attributed Metacritic
  scores. Multi-title releases retain their individual title IDs and versions.
- Catalog downloads can fall back to the GitHub contents API and the GitLab
  mirror. Cached snapshots and diffs are checked for provenance and age.
- Game details distinguish download size from the space required by selected
  packages, show title revisions, and link to the source topic through a QR code.
- File selection uses the available screen height, groups nested files, and
  warns about overlapping update selections before installation.

## Downloads and appearance

- Download cards show live peer statistics and retain network information while
  seeding. Secondary details can be expanded when needed.
- Verified pieces can be shared from RAM and SD storage. Peer discovery and
  incoming connections have received fixes.
- Uncached debrid torrents can remain in the provider queue.
- 7z archive header reads and writes no longer rely on unaligned integer
  pointer accesses.
- Added appearance themes and configurable accent colors. Theme changes apply
  after restarting pipensx.
- Added screen blanking during transfers and optional sleep after the queue
  finishes.

## Web Companion

- Manage downloads, browse the catalog and installed library, select files,
  change console settings, inspect logs, and run maintenance from a browser.
- Download a catalog through the phone or computer connection and upload it to
  the Switch. Local catalog JSON files are also supported, up to 48 MiB.
- Download the latest pipensx NRO and its checksum through the browser. The
  console verifies SHA-256 before staging the replacement.
- Upload a local NRO, then replace and restart through the existing updater.
  After the helper returns to HOME, launch pipensx again on the Switch.
- The update helper exits the application process, preventing forwarders from
  relaunching pipensx in the same loader session and crashing after replacement.
- Idle HTTP connections yield their slots to new requests, avoiding unnecessary
  busy responses while preserving active uploads and event streams.

Browser downloads use that device's connection, including its VPN. The VPN must
allow access to the Switch on the local network. If a source blocks browser
downloads through CORS, download the file separately and use the file picker.

## Installation

Copy `switch/pipensx/pipensx.nro` from `SDOut.zip` to the SD card, or replace the
existing NRO with the standalone `pipensx.nro`. Keep the existing pipensx data
directory to preserve settings, cached artwork, and download state. The public
build fetches its catalog on first use and does not bundle games or firmware.

Upgrading the published 1.6.6 build to 1.7.1 through Web Companion's NRO upload
and apply actions was tested on a physical Switch. The installed NRO checksum,
settings, and all six existing tasks were verified after the upgrade.

An older development build's helper did crash after replacement during a
separate test. If this happens, dismiss the error and launch pipensx again
from HOME; the file-copy method above is also available. Version 1.7.1 supplies
the corrected helper for subsequent updates.

packages.name: nx-fancontrol
packages.title: NX-FanControl
packages.description: Custom fan curve control.
packages.author: Zathawo, dominatorul
packages.details:
NX-FanControl is a sysmodule and overlay for customizing the console's internal fan curve.

It allows you to define multiple temperature points with corresponding fan speeds, giving you more control over the balance between cooling performance and fan noise. The overlay also provides real-time monitoring of SoC temperature and fan RPM.

Because NX-FanControl directly changes fan behavior, use sensible fan curves and avoid settings that significantly reduce cooling at high temperatures.
packages.changelog:
1.0.5+

Added

Support for 10 fan curve points, giving finer control over fan behavior.
SoC temperature and Fan Speed readings in the overlay.

Changed

Removed fan level change threshold — Fan speed now updates every cycle, giving immediate response to temperature or setting changes.

~Reduced sleep time from 500ms to 250ms — Updates 4 times per second, providing a more responsive experience while staying efficient.~

Optimized sleep state checking — System sleep is now checked every 20 iterations (~5 seconds) instead of every loop, reducing overhead while keeping power-saving functionality.

Fixed

Various minor bug fixes for improved stability and reliability.

Recompiled for latest Atmosphere support

2/13/2026

Reduced heap size from 512kb to 50kb. Now it uses 10x less memory.
Reduced sleep time to 50 ms and for temps over 50 degrees to 25ms.
Fixed critical config corruption bug: corrected fwrite/fread parameter order so fan curves now save/load properly.
Fixed fan speed not updating due to hysteresis logic: fan now updates immediately.
Removed unused variables causing Werror build failures.
